best_parts: node hA2: three options, each a different model (correct neck; TR14 complete obstruction; TR13 wide neck), each with a named wrong model and a refutation (fA2_t14, fA2_t13)
node bB1 / cC1: 'which step is wrong' with three steps, each carrying one trap; the classmate frame is a good exam-style check
node cC1: TR35 and TR21 both tested inside one caecal-volvulus stem; fC1_s3 explains why detorsion is not the end of care
flaws: node hA1 step 3 ('a femoral hernia needs early repair') is mapped to TR13, but its feedback (fA1_s3) argues 'rarity feels like safety', which is not TR13 (commonest equals most dangerous). Trap mapping and feedback disagree.
Objective gap: O9 is tested only for femoral and Richter. Littre (Meckel's) and Maydl (W-loop) are never probed, though the S5 goal names them.
Objective gap: O11 never asks for the caecum as perforation site in closed-loop large bowel obstruction, and O1 large bowel (TR35 as a commonest-cause stem) is never probed directly.
node eE1: two-option probe; the only trap is 'Adhesive band' and there is no hint or retry route, so a miss goes straight to the feedback.
node bB3 and cC2: two-option probes, each with one trap only; little choice for a learner who knows the rule.

best_parts: node theatre_case: the trap options are the real triggers a student reaches for (ultrasound confirmed; colicky pain and vomiting), and the key is the criterion (peritonitis); the feedback names the criterion, not the scan
node sites_case: both site qualifiers in one item (volvulus site versus perforation site), with the traps named as merged facts (sites_f_caecum)
node sig_case with sig_h_discharge and sig_h_hartmann: two different wrong models, each with a hint, a 'show me why' route and a sure_note that names the error
flaws: node virgin_case: two distractors ('Adhesive bands from an old operation' and 'Adhesive bands, the usual adult cause') are both TR2 and near-identical. The first is also dominated by the stem ('no previous surgery'), so a tired learner rejects it at once. The key is the only non-adhesion option, which is findable by form.
node femoral_mech_case: 'High frequency of the hernia in the population' is dominated by the key for any learner who has the concept. A two-option probe with one absurd option diagnoses nothing.
node lbo_f_volv: feedback ends 'Carcinoma is (K4).', a garbled sentence in an examiner-facing line.

node intus_case: the key ('Resection of the involved bowel') is the longest option and the only non-enema option, so it is findable by form. Same pattern in node intus_why_case, where the key is the longest option.
Hint ladder gaps: epon_case, lbo_case, sites_case, theatre_case and signs_case give a wrong pick the feedback with no retry, so no first-miss hint on those key probes (DP9).

best_parts: node g3 with g3_xA and g3_xB: the Richter, Littre and Maydl distinction is taught by a 'passing flatus, no vomiting' stem, and the sure_note names the mix-up
node g4 with g4_hR and g4_hM: each eponym's wrong content is refuted by its own hint and explanation (g4_xR, g4_xM)
node g8 with g8_x1 and g8_x2: the trap 'detorsion ends care' and the trap 'right hemicolectomy for any volvulus' each get a distinct, clean repair
flaws: Systematic telegraph (DP1): in all 13 probes (g1 to g13) the correct option is listed first. A learner can answer the whole segment by choosing option 1. Shuffle the key position.
node g2: two options only, and the trap ('High frequency in the population') is dominated by the key, so it diagnoses nothing.
node g3: the key ('Only part of the bowel wall is trapped, without full obstruction') is the longest option, another form cue.
node g6 and g5_ok: the trap 'Adults have the same idiopathic lead point as children' is self-contradictory, since 'idiopathic' means no known lead point. The wording is wrong for an examiner's trap.
node g7: both trap options ('Laparotomy, then manual reduction' and 'Laparotomy, since surgery is safer in a child') are TR4 near-duplicates, so the second adds nothing.

merge_ideas: b's virgin_case and femoral_case stems with c's Patient A versus Patient B contrast (g1) for the hernia block, one stem per learner decision.
c's eponym chain (g3 to g4, with per-content hints) plus Littre and Maydl probes added to b's femoral_mech_case, closing the O9 gap that a and b both leave.
b's theatre_case and sites_case items with c's hint and agency routes on every wrong pick, so no key probe is a dead miss.
a's classmate 'which step is wrong' format (hA1 and cC1) for the intussusception and volvulus stems, with step 3 of hA1 remapped to a real trap.
Shuffle the key position across all probes in the merged variant, and drop the dominated options ('from an old operation', 'High frequency').
